description: EURA CRA Compliance Rules Database - Generated from cra_rule_pack_v0.1.txt

rules.title: Security Policy Documentation
rules.description_short: Repository must have a SECURITY.md file for reporting security vulnerabilities.
rules.description_long: Your repository should have a SECURITY.md file (or equivalent) that explains how users can report security vulnerabilities. This demonstrates commitment to coordinated vulnerability disclosure, which CRA requires.

rules.title: Dependency Inventory (SBOM)
rules.description_short: Maintain an inventory of all dependencies for transparency in your product.
rules.description_long: You must maintain an inventory of all dependencies (Software Bill of Materials). CRA requires transparency about what components are in your product. Lockfiles and manifest files serve as a basic SBOM.

rules.title: Dependency Vulnerability Management
rules.description_short: Manage known vulnerabilities in dependencies to mitigate compliance risks.
rules.description_long: You must actively manage known vulnerabilities in dependencies. CRA requires that products address security issues promptly. Having vulnerable dependencies is a compliance risk.

rules.title: Secure Default Configuration
rules.description_short: Products should be secure-by-default with no unnecessary attack surface.
rules.description_long: Products should be secure-by-default. Default settings should not expose unnecessary attack surface. This includes: no default passwords, secure connection settings enabled by default, minimal permissions, etc.

rules.title: Update and Patch Management
rules.description_short: Process for providing security updates and patches to address vulnerabilities.
rules.description_long: CRA requires that products can be updated to address vulnerabilities. Evidence includes: release tags, changelog, update documentation.

references.note: Compliance with update and patch management requirements.

rules.title: Security Testing in CI/CD
rules.description_short: Automated security testing must be part of the CI/CD process to ensure proactive security validation.
rules.description_long: You should have automated security testing as part of your build/deployment process. This demonstrates proactive security validation, which CRA expects.

rules.title: Documentation of Security Features
rules.description_short: Products must provide adequate documentation for security-relevant features.
rules.description_long: Users must understand how to use your product securely. CRA requires that products provide adequate documentation. Security-relevant features should be documented.

rules.title: No Hardcoded Secrets
rules.description_short: Secrets must never be committed to version control to avoid security risks.
rules.description_long: Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens) must never be committed to version control. This is a fundamental security requirement and CRA violation risk. Applies to all repositories, especially those with CI/CD configurations where secrets often leak.

rules.title: Dependency Pinning and Reproducibility
rules.description_short: Dependencies must be pinned to specific versions to ensure reproducible builds.
rules.description_long: Dependencies should be pinned to specific versions (not '^1.0.0' or 'latest'). This ensures reproducible builds and prevents unexpected updates that could introduce vulnerabilities.

rules.title: Container Security (Dockerfile Best Practices)
rules.description_short: Containers must follow security best practices including non-root users and minimal base images.
rules.description_long: If you use containers (Docker), they should follow security best practices: non-root user, minimal base images, no secrets, health checks, etc. This demonstrates secure-by-design principles.

rules.title: Lifecycle Management Evidence
rules.description_short: Demonstrate active maintenance and lifecycle plan for your product.
rules.description_long: You must demonstrate that your product is actively maintained and has a lifecycle plan. CRA requires products to be supported throughout their lifecycle. Evidence includes: recent commits, maintenance status, deprecation notices if applicable.

rules.title: Access Control Documentation
rules.description_short: Documentation of authentication and authorization features is required for secure access control configuration.
rules.description_long: If your product has authentication/authorization features, they must be documented. Users need to understand how to configure access controls securely. CRA requires adequate documentation of security features.

rules.title: Encryption and Data Protection
rules.description_short: Sensitive data must be encrypted and documented to ensure data protection.
rules.description_long: If your product handles sensitive data, encryption should be used and documented. CRA requires appropriate security measures for data protection. Evidence includes: encryption configuration, TLS/SSL settings, data protection documentation.

rules.title: Incident Response Preparation
rules.description_short: Documentation on handling security incidents is required for preparedness.
rules.description_long: You should have documentation about how security incidents are handled. While CRA's incident reporting is primarily organizational, having documentation in the repo shows preparedness.

rules.title: Build and Deployment Security
rules.description_short: Ensure secure build and deployment processes throughout the product lifecycle.
rules.description_long: Your build and deployment process should be secure. This includes secure CI/CD configuration, signed artifacts, and secure deployment procedures. CRA expects security throughout the product lifecycle.

rules.title: Third-Party Component Assessment
rules.description_short: Assess third-party components for security and compliance.
rules.description_long: You should assess third-party components (dependencies) for security and compliance. CRA requires knowing what's in your product. Having a process for dependency assessment demonstrates due diligence.

rules.title: Version and Release Management
rules.description_short: Identify product versions and changes to support vulnerability management.
rules.description_long: You must be able to identify which version of your product is deployed and what changes are in each version. This supports vulnerability management and update processes required by CRA.

references.article: CRA Article 11 - Version identification for updates

rules.title: Secure Communication Documentation
rules.description_short: Secure communication (TLS/HTTPS) must be required and documented for networked products.
rules.description_long: If your product communicates over networks, secure communication (TLS/HTTPS) should be required and documented. CRA requires secure-by-design, which includes secure network communication.

rules.title: Input Validation and Sanitization
rules.description_short: Products must validate and sanitize all external inputs to prevent injection attacks.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 10 requires products to be designed with appropriate cybersecurity measures. Input validation is a fundamental security control that prevents injection attacks (SQL, XSS, command injection). Evidence includes validation libraries in dependencies, input sanitization configuration, or security linting rules.

references.note: Products shall ensure input validation to prevent exploitation

rules.title: Authentication and Identity Management
rules.description_short: Products with user access must implement proper authentication and identity controls.
rules.description_long: CRA requires access control mechanisms appropriate to the risk. Products should implement authentication (e.g., OAuth, JWT, API keys) and document how identity is managed. Evidence includes auth configuration files, identity provider setup, and auth documentation.

rules.title: Least Privilege and Minimal Attack Surface
rules.description_short: Products must apply least privilege principles and minimize their attack surface.
rules.description_long: CRA requires products to minimize attack surface. For containerized applications, this means using non-root users, minimal base images, dropping capabilities, and using .dockerignore. For all products, it means documenting permission requirements and following least-privilege principles.

references.note: Minimize attack surface and apply least privilege

rules.title: Secure Error Handling and Logging
rules.description_short: Products must handle errors securely and implement appropriate logging without leaking sensitive information.
rules.description_long: CRA requires products to be resilient and secure in failure modes. Error messages must not expose internal details (stack traces, database queries, file paths) to end users. Security-relevant events must be logged for audit purposes. Evidence includes logging configuration, error handling policies, and debug mode settings.

references.note: Secure error handling and security event logging

rules.title: Cryptographic Implementation Standards
rules.description_short: Products must use up-to-date, industry-standard cryptographic methods.
rules.description_long: CRA Annex I requires products to protect data using state-of-the-art cryptography. Products must use TLS 1.2+ for communication, strong encryption algorithms, proper key management, and document their cryptographic approach. Deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES) must not be used for security purposes.

rules.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Process
rules.description_short: Products must have a documented coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 11 mandates that manufacturers establish a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy. SECURITY.md must include: how to report vulnerabilities, expected response timeline, scope of accepted reports, safe harbour statement, and contact information. This rule verifies disclosure process completeness beyond mere file existence (CRA-BASE-001).

rules.title: Security Advisory Publication
rules.description_short: Manufacturers must publish security advisories for known vulnerabilities.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 11(2) requires timely notification of vulnerabilities to users and authorities (ENISA). Products should have a mechanism for publishing security advisories. Evidence includes GitHub security advisory templates, advisory publication workflow, or advisory documentation.

references.note: Vulnerability notification to users and ENISA

rules.title: Vulnerability Tracking and Triage
rules.description_short: Products must have a system for tracking, triaging, and managing reported vulnerabilities.
rules.description_long: CRA requires manufacturers to maintain records of vulnerabilities and remediation actions. A vulnerability tracking system (issue tracker, security-specific templates) demonstrates organized handling. Evidence includes security bug report templates, vulnerability tracking documentation, or integration with CVE databases.

rules.title: Patch Delivery Timeline Compliance
rules.description_short: Security patches must be delivered without undue delay, with defined SLAs.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 11(4) requires manufacturers to address vulnerabilities without undue delay and provide patches free of charge. Products should document patch delivery timelines, have release automation for rapid deployment, and demonstrate evidence of timely patch history. SLAs: critical within 24-72 hours, high within 7 days.

references.note: Timely patch delivery without undue delay

rules.title: User Security Configuration Guide
rules.description_short: Products must provide a security configuration guide for end users.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 13 requires products to be accompanied by clear documentation enabling users to securely configure and use the product. This includes a security hardening guide, default credential changes, network exposure minimization, and feature-specific security settings.

rules.title: API Security Documentation
rules.description_short: Products with APIs must document their interfaces including security considerations.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 13(6) requires documentation of product interfaces. APIs must be documented with security considerations including authentication requirements, rate limiting, input constraints, and error responses. Evidence includes OpenAPI specifications, API documentation, or interface security guides.

rules.title: Architecture and Threat Model Documentation
rules.description_short: Products must document their security architecture and threat model.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 13(2) requires technical documentation that includes a general description of the product design. A security architecture document and threat model demonstrate security-by-design. Evidence includes architecture diagrams, threat analysis, data flow documentation, and security design documents.

references.note: Product design and security architecture documentation

rules.title: Secure Installation and Deployment Guide
rules.description_short: Products must include secure installation and deployment instructions.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 13(3) requires instructions for secure installation and deployment. Users must be able to install, configure, and operate the product securely from initial setup. Evidence includes installation guides with security steps, deployment checklists, and infrastructure-as-code with security configurations.

rules.title: End-of-Life and Support Policy
rules.description_short: Products must have a documented support period and end-of-life policy.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 12(1) requires manufacturers to determine and document the expected product lifetime and support period. Users must know how long they can expect security updates. Evidence includes support policy documentation, EOL timeline, and maintenance commitment statements.

references.note: Product support period and EOL policy

rules.title: Active Maintenance Evidence
rules.description_short: Products must demonstrate active maintenance through regular updates and activity.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 12(2) requires manufacturers to maintain products throughout the support period. Evidence of active maintenance includes recent commits, regular dependency updates, resolved issues, and maintenance status indicators. Repositories with no updates for 180+ days may indicate abandonment.

rules.title: Update Notification and Distribution
rules.description_short: Products must have mechanisms to notify users of security updates and distribute patches.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 12(3) requires manufacturers to inform users about security updates and provide automatic update mechanisms where possible. Evidence includes release automation workflows, notification systems, update documentation, and subscription mechanisms (RSS, mailing list, GitHub releases).

rules.title: Backward Compatibility and Migration Support
rules.description_short: Products must provide migration guidance and manage backward compatibility during updates.
rules.description_long: CRA Article 12(4) requires that updates do not negatively impact the security of the product. When breaking changes are necessary, migration guides, deprecation notices, and upgrade paths must be documented to ensure users can transition securely. Evidence includes migration documentation, deprecation policies, and version upgrade guides.

references.note: Secure update transition and backward compatibility

REM-001.description:
Create Security Policy Document
- Action: Create SECURITY.md file in repository root or .github/ directory
- Template: Include contact email, response time commitment, scope of
  vulnerabilities to report
- Verification: File exists and contains security contact information
- Timeline: Can be done immediately (1 hour)

REM-002.description:
Implement Dependency Lockfiles
- Action: Generate and commit dependency lockfiles (package-lock.json,
  Pipfile.lock, etc.)
- Tools: npm install, pipenv lock, poetry lock
- Verification: Lockfile exists and is committed to version control
- Timeline: Immediate for existing projects, ongoing for new dependencies

REM-003.description:
Set Up Dependency Vulnerability Scanning
- Action: Integrate vulnerability scanning into development workflow
- Tools: npm audit, pip-audit, Snyk, Dependabot, OWASP Dependency-Check
- Verification: Scanning runs automatically (CI/CD or pre-commit)
- Timeline: 1-2 days for setup, ongoing monitoring

REM-004.description:
Remove Hardcoded Secrets
- Action: Audit codebase for secrets, remove them, rotate exposed secrets
- Tools: git-secrets, truffleHog, gitleaks, GitGuardian
- Verification: No secrets detected in scans, .env in .gitignore
- Timeline: Immediate (rotate secrets), 1 day for cleanup

REM-005.description:
Implement Secure Defaults
- Action: Review and update default configurations to be secure
- Steps: Remove default passwords, use environment variables, add .env.example
- Verification: No secrets in config files, secure defaults documented
- Timeline: 1-2 days depending on config complexity

REM-006.description:
Add Security Testing to CI/CD
- Action: Add security scanning steps to CI/CD pipeline
- Tools: CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit, Snyk, OWASP ZAP
- Verification: Security tests run on every PR/commit
- Timeline: 2-3 days for initial setup

REM-007.description:
Create Security Documentation
- Action: Add security section to README and/or create dedicated security docs
- Content: Security features, secure configuration, vulnerability reporting
- Verification: Documentation exists and is accessible
- Timeline: 1 day for initial documentation

REM-008.description:
Implement Dependency Pinning
- Action: Pin all dependencies to exact versions, commit lockfiles
- Tools: Update manifest files, generate lockfiles
- Verification: No version ranges in manifests, lockfiles committed
- Timeline: 1 day for existing projects

REM-009.description:
Secure Dockerfile Configuration
- Action: Update Dockerfile to use non-root user, minimal base image
- Steps: Add USER directive, switch to alpine/distroless base, add HEALTHCHECK
- Verification: Dockerfile follows security best practices
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-010.description:
Document Update and Patch Process
- Action: Create CHANGELOG.md and document update procedures
- Content: How to update, version history, update notifications
- Verification: CHANGELOG exists, update process documented
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-011.description:
Establish Lifecycle Management
- Action: Document maintenance status and lifecycle policy
- Content: Support duration, maintenance schedule, EOL policy
- Verification: Lifecycle information in README or docs
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-012.description:
Document Access Controls
- Action: Create authentication/authorization documentation
- Content: How auth works, how to configure, security considerations
- Verification: Auth documentation exists
- Timeline: 1-2 days depending on complexity

REM-013.description:
Document Encryption Approach
- Action: Document how encryption is used in the product
- Content: Encryption at rest, in transit, key management
- Verification: Encryption documentation exists
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-014.description:
Create Incident Response Documentation
- Action: Add incident response section to SECURITY.md
- Content: How to report, response timeline, contact information
- Verification: Incident response info in SECURITY.md
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-015.description:
Secure Build and Deployment
- Action: Review and secure CI/CD configuration
- Steps: Use secrets management, add security checks, document process
- Verification: CI/CD uses secrets, no hardcoded credentials
- Timeline: 2-3 days

REM-016.description:
Establish Dependency Assessment Process
- Action: Document dependency selection and approval process
- Content: Assessment criteria, approval workflow
- Verification: Dependency policy document exists
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-017.description:
Implement Version Management
- Action: Add version tracking and use semantic versioning
- Steps: Add version to code, use git tags, create CHANGELOG
- Verification: Version is trackable, releases are tagged
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-018.description:
Document Secure Communication Requirements
- Action: Document TLS/HTTPS requirements
- Content: TLS version requirements, certificate management
- Verification: Secure communication documented
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-019.description:
Implement Input Validation
- Action: Add input validation and sanitization for all external inputs
- Steps: Use validation libraries (Joi, Cerberus, Pydantic), add schema validation for APIs, sanitize HTML/SQL inputs
- Tools: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet, ESLint security plugins
- Verification: All API endpoints validate input; no raw user input reaches queries
- Timeline: 2-5 days

REM-020.description:
Implement Authentication Controls
- Action: Add authentication and identity management
- Steps: Implement OAuth2/JWT/session-based auth, document auth flow, add MFA support
- Tools: Passport.js, python-jose, Auth0, Keycloak
- Verification: All protected endpoints require authentication; auth flow documented
- Timeline: 3-7 days

REM-021.description:
Apply Least Privilege Principle
- Action: Review and minimize permissions throughout the product
- Steps: Add USER directive to Dockerfiles, drop unnecessary Linux capabilities, use minimal base images, add .dockerignore
- Verification: Containers run as non-root; documented permission requirements
- Timeline: 1-2 days

REM-022.description:
Implement Secure Error Handling
- Action: Add structured logging and secure error handling
- Steps: Replace generic exceptions with specific handlers, mask sensitive data in logs, disable debug mode in production, configure structured logging
- Tools: structlog, Winston, Serilog, log4j2
- Verification: No stack traces in production responses; sensitive data masked in logs
- Timeline: 2-3 days

REM-023.description:
Configure Cryptographic Standards
- Action: Audit and update cryptographic implementation
- Steps: Require TLS 1.2+, disable weak cipher suites, use AES-256 for encryption at rest, document key management
- Tools: SSLyze, testssl.sh, Mozilla SSL Configuration Generator
- Verification: No deprecated algorithms; TLS properly configured; key management documented
- Timeline: 2-3 days

REM-024.description:
Establish Vulnerability Disclosure Process
- Action: Create comprehensive SECURITY.md with CVD policy
- Content: How to report (email, form), response timeline (acknowledge in 48h, fix SLA), scope, safe harbour statement, PGP key
- Standards: ISO 29147 (Vulnerability Disclosure), RFC 9116 (security.txt)
- Verification: SECURITY.md exists with complete CVD process
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-025.description:
Set Up Security Advisory Publication
- Action: Create security advisory workflow
- Steps: Enable GitHub Security Advisories, create advisory template, set up notification workflow
- Content: CVE ID, affected versions, severity, mitigation steps, patched version
- Verification: Advisory template exists; process documented
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-026.description:
Implement Vulnerability Tracking
- Action: Set up vulnerability tracking system
- Steps: Create security-specific issue templates, define triage process, establish severity classification (CVSS)
- Tools: GitHub Issues, Jira Security, dedicated vulnerability tracker
- Verification: Security issue template exists; triage process documented
- Timeline: 1-2 days

REM-027.description:
Define Patch Delivery SLA
- Action: Document and automate patch delivery timelines
- SLAs: Critical 24-72 hours, High 7 days, Medium 30 days, Low next release
- Steps: Create release automation, document release process, add deployment pipeline
- Verification: Release workflow exists; SLA documented; recent patches meet SLA
- Timeline: 2-3 days

REM-028.description:
Create User Security Guide
- Action: Write user-facing security configuration documentation
- Content: Secure configuration checklist, credential management, network settings, feature-specific security, hardening steps
- Verification: Security guide exists and covers key configuration areas
- Timeline: 1-2 days

REM-029.description:
Document API Security
- Action: Create API documentation with security considerations
- Steps: Generate OpenAPI spec, document auth requirements per endpoint, rate limits, input constraints
- Tools: Swagger/OpenAPI, Redoc, Stoplight
- Verification: OpenAPI spec exists; security schemes documented
- Timeline: 2-3 days

REM-030.description:
Create Architecture Documentation
- Action: Document security architecture and threat model
- Content: Component diagram, data flow, trust boundaries, threat analysis (STRIDE), mitigation strategies
- Tools: draw.io, Mermaid, Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool
- Verification: Architecture document and threat model exist
- Timeline: 2-5 days

REM-031.description:
Create Installation Security Guide
- Action: Write secure installation and deployment instructions
- Content: Prerequisites, step-by-step install, security configuration, environment variables, firewall rules, TLS setup
- Verification: Installation guide with security steps exists
- Timeline: 1-2 days

REM-032.description:
Define End-of-Life Policy
- Action: Document product support period and EOL policy
- Content: Support duration (minimum 5 years per CRA), maintenance schedule, EOL notification process, migration path at EOL
- Verification: Support policy document exists with clear timelines
- Timeline: 1 day

REM-033.description:
Demonstrate Active Maintenance
- Action: Establish and show ongoing maintenance
- Steps: Enable Dependabot/Renovate, maintain regular commit cadence, update dependencies, respond to issues
- Verification: Recent commits within 90 days; automated dependency updates enabled
- Timeline: 1 day for initial setup, ongoing

REM-034.description:
Set Up Update Notifications
- Action: Create update notification and distribution mechanism
- Steps: Enable GitHub Releases, create release workflow, add changelog automation, consider mailing list or RSS
- Tools: semantic-release, release-drafter, GitHub Actions
- Verification: Release workflow automated; users can subscribe to updates
- Timeline: 1-2 days

REM-035.description:
Create Migration Guide
- Action: Document version migration paths and backward compatibility policy
- Content: Breaking change policy, migration steps between major versions, deprecation notices with timeline, automated migration scripts
- Verification: Migration guide exists for recent major versions
- Timeline: 1-2 days per major version
